paper.core_task: Robust distributed learning with Byzantine workers under data heterogeneity

contributions.name: An adaptive robust clipping scheme for gradient aggregation
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose ARC, wherein prior to aggregating the gradients, the server clips the largest k := ⌊2(f /n)(n -f )⌋ gradients using a clipping parameter given by the (Euclidean) norm of the (k + 1)-th largest gradient.
contributions.description: A pre-aggregation gradient clipping method that dynamically sets the clipping threshold based on the sorted norms of worker gradients and the adversarial fraction, requiring no additional prior information.

contributions.name: An improved robustness guarantee under bounded initialization
contributions.author_claim_text: We demonstrate that ARC constrains the norm of an adversarial gradient by that of an honest (non-adversarial) gradient. contributions.description: A theoretical analysis showing ARC improves convergence guarantees over standard robust aggregation methods when model initialization is good, breaking a known lower bound.

novelty_claims.text: ARC offers a practical solution for gradient clipping in distributed learning, enhancing robustness without sacrificing theoretical guarantees.
